weaknesses.rationale: The email parameter is directly embedded into a JSON payload sent to a backend that may query a NoSQL database like MongoDB, potentially allowing operator injection via special keys like $ne or $regex.

weaknesses.title: NoSQL Injection — query filtering via `name` parameter (GET /api/Challenges/)
weaknesses.rationale: The `name` parameter may be passed unsanitized into a NoSQL query, allowing operators like `$where` or `$ne` to manipulate logic.

weaknesses.title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) — Socket.IO session identifier param `sid` (POST /socket.io/)
weaknesses.rationale: The `sid` parameter directly references a specific session and might allow unauthorized access to other users' sessions if predictable or guessable.

weaknesses.title: IDOR — object reference via query param `name` (GET /api/Challenges/)
weaknesses.rationale: If `name` maps to an internal object identifier used without authorization checks, changing it may expose other users' challenge data.

weaknesses.title: Server Side Request Forgery (SSRF) — Socket.IO polling transport param `transport` (POST /socket.io/)
weaknesses.rationale: The `transport=polling` parameter influences how the server handles socket communication, potentially leading to SSRF if user-controlled transport options are used for internal requests.

weaknesses.title: SSRF — query param `transport` (GET /socket.io/)
weaknesses.rationale: The `transport` parameter influences internal connection mechanisms and might lead to unintended server-side requests if improperly validated.

weaknesses.title: SSRF — server-side fetch triggered by `name` parameter (GET /api/Challenges/)
weaknesses.rationale: If the backend uses the `name` value to initiate a server-side HTTP request (e.g., to fetch metadata), it could be coerced into accessing internal services.

weaknesses.title: Prototype Pollution — Socket.IO session ID param `sid` (POST /socket.io/)

weaknesses.title: HTTP Parameter Pollution — Multiple query params (`EIO`, `transport`, `t`, `sid`) (POST /socket.io/)

weaknesses.title: Denial of Service (DoS) via Socket.IO Flooding — Polling transport with session params (POST /socket.io/)
